facts.label: Present perfect com just, already e yet
facts.sub: Use have/has + particípio. Just e already ficam antes do particípio; yet vai no fim de perguntas e negativas: Have you finished yet? Not yet.

facts.label: Acabou de
facts.sub: Use have/has + just + particípio para algo muito recente: I’ve just left the office. Just fica entre have e o particípio. Mostra que a ação acabou há poucos minutos.

facts.label: Já
facts.sub: Use already para dizer que algo está feito: She has already sent it. Fica entre have/has e o particípio. Também aparece em perguntas: Have you already told them?

compare.ask: I’ve just got a new job.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “acabei de chegar” e “já fiz”, e o verbo fica no passado.
compare.tip: Diga: “I’ve just got a new job.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use have/has + particípio: I’ve just arrived. I’ve already done it. Nas perguntas e negativas, use yet no fim.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Just means a very short time ago.
Yet is used in affirmative sentences about the past.
items.why: Yet is used in questions and negatives.

items.s: Already shows that something is done earlier than expected.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Just means a very short time ago. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Yet is used in affirmative sentences about the past. → Falso (Yet is used in questions and negatives.)
Already shows that something is done earlier than expected. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A busy Chicago office · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a busy Monday morning in an office in Chicago. Phones ring and keyboards click everywhere. Al has just come out of the boss’s office. He is smiling, and his hands shake a little. His colleague Eva has already finished her emails. She sees his face and walks over.
“Eva, guess what? My boss has just offered me a new job!” says Al. “Really? Have you already told your family?” says Eva. “Not yet. I’ve only told you. I’ve just left her office.” says Al.
